title: Morton's personality and what other musicians said of him
summary: Fats Pichon's hostile view versus Bunk Johnson, Simeon and Baby Dodds's respect for Morton.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I'd like to know what your personal opinion of his personality was.

I'm like, I believe, with all the musicians, and most of the better ones, you'll hear some awful reports occasionally, some musicians will say, oh, he was terrible. For instance, when we went to try to get, when Bunk came here in 1942, we went down to see Fats Pichon, Walter Pichon, who's probably a very nice guy, and I was prejudiced against him because when Bunk went and asked him to record with him, he refused. I guess it was going to be a non-union date. The union, of course, meant nothing to Bunk and all. I guess Walter was in the union and didn't want to do it, but the Bunk union, nothing meant anything except music in the first place and then friendship. I mean, Bunk was a 100% man. You hear all these awful sloppy stuff all about Bunk. It's disgusting to me. It doesn't really make much difference because nobody knows who he is hardly anymore, but I mean, Bunk was a wonderful guy. Bunk, if he was a friend, he'd do anything for you. I mean, you didn't have to be in the union to record or anything else if he wanted to record with somebody. But I mean, he didn't care if he was put out of the union. If some of his friends was going to do something, that's it. So he couldn't understand why Walter would have turned him down. I remember Walter at that time was talking something about Jelly Roll and running him down pretty much, or Jelly was just sort of a gangster who had a gun. And he was the only one that, Walter was the only one that Jelly was afraid of. Jelly, I think he claimed he put Jelly in his place once. Anyway, as if he was a very undesirable character, you know. He probably knew Jelly under some bad circumstances in New York, you know, when they didn't get along. But I mean, otherwise, I can't think of anybody, really any musician that, who I would call a musician, that ever knocked Jelly. There probably are some, and maybe I've heard things like that before, that he was hard to get along with, and that he bragged too much and talked too much. Some of them will laugh about that he was such a big talker. But practically everybody, like Simeon and all, say, no, I didn't see anything hard to get along with. Baby does, no, he was very businesslike and knew what he wanted, and he maybe would make Johnny play in the low register. Maybe he made Baby play with brushes when Baby didn't want to, but they wouldn't talk back to him. They had all sorts of respect for him. Like, as I mentioned, Judy Singleton. He wouldn't, no, I wouldn't be later, not with Jelly.
